title: Complexity of satisfiable word equations
context:
Finite descriptions of languages and transformations. Questions concern expressive power, decidability, and the cost of changing representations.

This source asks whether ordinary word-equation satisfiability is in NP. The transferred question concerns plain equations over free monoids, without adding regular constraints or inversion.

The 2026 source again identifies NP membership of ordinary word-equation satisfiability as a frontier. It is retained with the plain-equation convention of this question.

The recompression survey discusses the complexity of plain word-equation satisfiability alongside extensions. Only its plain-equation question is consolidated here; regular-constraint extensions are not declared equivalent.

sentences: A word equation equates two sequences containing letters and variables that stand for finite strings.
Satisfiability asks whether a consistent substitution makes the two resulting strings identical.
The project seeks the computational complexity of this decision problem, sharpening the gap between NP-hardness and polynomial-space algorithms recorded in the sources.
Substituted strings can be much larger than the equation, so an efficient algorithm must reason about their structure implicitly.
Understanding this cost would clarify the algorithmic difficulty of one of the simplest exact string-solving tasks.
